notes: Bathes in emotional, peaking waters for the first 10 minutes before Nick goes double time, settling into a rocky hot spring that overlooks a cosmic dawn, with a flock of birds migrating -> Todd's Tots.
Stays straightforward for the first half before crawling into a damp, semi-aquatic bog, where its groove echoes with deep blues and yellows, eventually sliding into sunlight and -> Salamander Song.

Drifts out to the coast and wades patiently in the sunlight before night falls, cruising past distant geometric lights that revolve and shutter in a kind of mechanical photosynthesis as they make their way toward the city. Pretty Walls-y at times.
Burrows into a dark, funky subway station, eventually bursting with energetic light.
Moves through light, Cory-led territory before swirling into outer space, orbiting patiently, then shifting into a bright, emotional gear that propels them to a close. Very Fuel-ish.
Hard-hitting Shon throughout, with an In the Eyes of Thieves feel at times.
Bubbles with static before curving down a swirling tunnel at twilight, eventually shooting through the strait to a close.

Flutters lightly before embarking on a zero-gravity walk above forested streams, skipping happily over pockets of air through the valley before reaching a gloomy, slow-motion waterfall set ablaze, dipping into -> Dirtbath.
Slightly chaotic, with an old-school Spafford sound.
Boogies harder than usual and builds nicely.

Descends into the inner workings of a city, passing underground windows of mechanized operations as robots shift through the glass and chase it to the peak. The final third wanders and wobbles a bit, but the last two minutes open up spaciously and build cleanly -> Night After Night.
Keeps watch over a harbor as ships with blaring lights stream and shuffle below, while a bridge shifts and locks into different positions, eventually opening up to a bay beneath a fiery sunset.

Flies through space with sharp synths for the first jam before landing on a Funkadelic planet in the second, where it hovers and surveils, slowly rotating into dawn as clouds timelapse through shifting hues. Patient-er than patient.
Deliciously space rodeo opera-y.
Coasts on a cool groove and has some ominous organ.
A riverboat western take on the song itself sprouts a swampy, funky jam that twinkles its way toward -> Levilan Shores.
Patiently makes its way to a nice, bright peak.
Glides through space with ease in a straightforward manner -> Peaches.
A bright take on an Anyone-esque groove that (no way!) gets trance-y and swings into a colorful jam that slides smoothly into -> Down Under.
Video game racing with a wish-washy sound throughout.
Skips from star to star inside of a disco-ball universe.
Breaks orbit and transitions smoothly -> Anyone.
Sits in a cyberpunk wind tunnel.

Moves through and alongside a projection of millions of years of activity before diving in and breaking through the atmosphere with its systems working overtime. Once it bursts through the clouds, it settles into a new, funky, bluesy, low-key groove that drifts around the horizon of a volcanic island, progressively bubbling into -> Virtual Bean Dip.
Makes its way to an Art Deco coastline at night before bursting brightly.
Robotic funk that grows with a dirty undertone.
Sort of has three parts to it: starts with standard Funkadelic, then a polished, glossy groove pops up and melts into wavy playing that swings into -> The Way You Do the Things You Do.
Straightforward, feel-good jam with incredible peaks.

song: The Way You Do the Things You Do
notes: Orbits patiently.
Boogies around the world and has a killer first buildup.
Surveils intergalactic glacial volcanoes.
Hits double-time space with a false buildup, then drops into a heavy groove and an intense peak.

Rolls through Acadian countryside and sets up camp at twilight, with beams of light falling from above, eventually lighting up the landscape. From there, the second jam swirls into a spacey, speedy, New Wave bopping groove that gets gooier as it slows and snappier as it quickens into -> Darkness Singularity.
Relaxed, cool groove with slippery synths that morphs into a cyclical trance before building into -> Stuck in the Middle with You.
Acts as a shooting star, blazing across space with color before slowing into orbit with a happy, bluesy groove that stutters and sharpens into -> Fake the Fate.
Groove-oriented, but largely same-y throughout. Great Shon with a fiery ending, though.
Grooves slickly at Shon's insistence, like Luther Vandross and Huey Lewis in molasses, before building intently for a nasty ending.
Awesome, spacey synths and an emotional ending.

song: Stuck in the Middle with You
notes: Spins through universes upon universes -> Dis Go In 5?
Robotic whisperings during a rainbow, full-body scan aboard a spaceship bursts into a dance tutorial.
Consonant, entrancing groove with heated peaks that cool into a lush stream -> Palisades.
Cools into a remote, semi-frozen northern lake at the turn from Winter to Spring, where they tinker with mechanics and happily skip across the water.
Resident spaceship band detours through the American Midwest, slips into deep space, and rockets toward -> Alternate Ending.
Direct, mechanical groove that slips into serene space just above the clouds, peaking brightly before fluttering away.
Moves through a cosmic nature preserve before emerging into an aquatic sunrise.
A loose take on Echoes goes 90s R&B mode and slips into deep, groovy space before sliding out of view.
Grooves steadily and robotically before peaking nicely and dipping into very deep space for the last few minutes.
Peaks early, then calms into a funky rhythm that gradually builds.

A look into an Artic landscape, beginning with a lone deer foraging, then splitting into hundreds of rainbow reflections endlessly leaping through the air, eventually calming into a placid, nocturnal lake that turns funky and works its way with pace and brightness to -> All My Friends.
Spacious, patient, Night After Night-ish jamming that turns upbeat.
Standard first half, with some Funkadelic-y jamming and sparse playing that rolls together beautifully.
Short, with a nice, rough edge to it.
Straightforward, slightly industrial playing with loud, hard-hitting bass.
Spacey, yacht rock groove that builds smoothly to a close.
The first jam flutters and revolves gracefully, while the second dives into a heavy, funky stomp.
Crystals refracting light guide the way to a fun, Cory-led groove.
Glides through space, hopping from planet to planet with ease before moving into Salamander Song-esque territory that blends into Cantaloupe Island.
Excavates through dark caves before breaking through angelically into celebratory space - very Anyone-ish - then drops into some heavy funk in the final minutes.
Standard Echoes-y jamming that drifts into a Latin Space Gadget-y groove.
Swirls nicely with determined playing.
Flow-state run through.
Slightly spacey at times but stays Type I throughout.
Absorbs into a beautiful groove that coasts smoothly before sliding into Walls-y territory that calms and simmers.
Glides gracefully across a lake at twilight before spinning itself into a star.
Tribal beginnings give way to slick futuristic grooving that builds cleanly, peaks early, and has a few minutes of extra playing tacked on the end.
Great rave atmosphere.
Desert heat ray grooving with a clean ending.
Major Bootsy Collins vibes.
Nice, slick, washy groove pops up.
Patiently moves through spacey waters before peaking, then spends a few moments working its way -> Night After Night.
Slips into a spacey groove where blues and oranges bounce against each other.
Hikes through beautiful Albertan wilderness.
Heavy, spacey funk with an ending straight out of Darkness Singularity.
Cyclical, colorful jamming that hums, vibrates, and flares with life.
Bounces colorfully inside an invisible dome.
Awesome full-band grooving that makes its way into an intergalactic jungle.
Sits on the crest of Earth’s horizon at sunrise. Real Red-sounding ending, too.
Fantastically terse, upbeat, and direct playing. Timing is incorrect as the recording got cut off.
Super polished grooving that ramps into a higher gear.
Determined funk bursts into bright space with some spectacular guitar work.
Effervescent, bubbling groove that twangs into spacey, almost Aliens-y territory.
Short as can be, with an inspired solo from Brian.
Yes! 17:02! A smooth solo from Cory with tons of teases makes for a nice outing, then nearly 10 more minutes of fluid, dancey grooving are tacked on.
Debut. Feel good, type 1 jam that bobs and rocks with awesome Shon throughout.

Zooms in on a passengerless, inconspicuously militarized ship drifting through a vast sea that sprays rainbow liquid crystals, paving glossy pathways it boogies down, eventually crashing and slipping into emotional, guitar-driven space, before sliding into the sunrise.
Meanders through a forest picking flowers before witnessing an alien abduction, having its memory wiped, and dancing its way home.

Emotionally driven, polished guitar makes for a superb outing of the song itself before rolling into a circular groove that grows brighter until it drops into syncopated, synth-led territory where Shon (!) goes off as Cory builds them into an astro-brew trading post turned laser jump rope rave.
A bit of Plinko here.
Hard-hitting bass, strong synth work, and speedy guitar make for a solid outing.
A willing participant in a video-game race that flies off the track and into nocturnal, patient space, before some shredding from Brian and a few surprisingly groovy closing minutes.
A glimpse into the future with some progressive, minimalistic, slightly electronic jamming.

Quickly slips into a tunnel where each instrument rotates, connects, and swirls around the others as a physically deep IMAG visualization, transforming the tunnel into a landscape of millions of trees angularly expanding and breathing in time, before a customary ending.
Slippery, funky, synth-driven jam.
Jazzy grand piano work from Cory floats over routine funk and grows spacious, slightly synthy, and robust.

An unusually minimalistic initial buildup bursts into rich, staccato jamming that glides and jump-ropes through vibrant, wonky space, building brightly before swinging out of orbit and into an array of line-dancing stars.
Crawls out of a shimmering stream and ramps up funkily in its second half.
Asymmetrical, mirrored hopscotch.
Groovy throughout, with a cool glide into gloomier space before spiking into VBD.
An energetic maze.
Sharp hues converge in a metallic polar dream, racing down icy mountainsides and cliff diving through montages of outer space glimpses.
Slick, vibrant wonderland.
Repetitive, deep funk driven by a slapping Shon.
An extra couple minutes of spacey goodness tucked in here.
Spacious, dub-y, and trudges through sludge in its final third.
A synth-forward endeavor that pokes and prods over looping structures, growing funkier before warming into Electro-Rock and working its way into Darkness Singularity with a starlit buildup.
An extension of the previous night’s Ginger Stardust, this one gets down early with unrelenting funk, moves through a brief patch of Plinko, and gradually fades out of view.
Slick grooving with twinges of jazzy blues that ramps up energetically -> America.
An early ’90s home exercise soundtrack takes a turn -> The Other One.

A superb outing for the song itself opens into concentrated, bright playing that each member, especially Brian, swirls around and weaves through with precision and energy before slipping into a low-key, lightly entrancing groove that rocks back up to a celebratory peak.
Bouncing, springy New Wave.
Cool, bluesy grooving that speeds through Pop Reggae before exploding into a peak.

The first jam features some Evil-ish (The Evil!) playing from Brian and Cory before sliding into a second jam ripped straight out of The Postman, with a few minutes of grooving that ramps up and then fades toward Anyone at its tail end.
Gooey, lava-lamp, almost Hood-like jamming that builds cleanly.
Gradually veers off the road and slips onto an unmarked galactic exit.

Boogies into a breathing city at astronomical twilight, floating past steaming shops and visualizations of previous and parallel universes, only to find itself back where it began, triggering a frantic exit attempt.
Jazzy overtones over a funky foundation tightly wind themselves into a bouncing, electronic ball that unfurls into a celebratory final section, with Cory going all out on the grand piano.
Fun, type 1 grooving that slips into deep, spacious reggae before closing out.
Gradually sinks underwater until it phases into a dark corridor that thumps with each internal wave.
Soars brightly and beautifully.
Sticks to slick synths before a celebratory close.
A rumbling nightclub boxed in by darkness, with its eastern wall slowly dissipating with the sunrise.

Bobbles through pristine Appalachian wilderness, staying on a funky interfluve between twin rivers that branch and converge in celebratory fashion before a solar eclipse darkens the scene, with the interfluve slipping backward as the rivers freeze in place, unveiling a landscape of thousands of breathing, glimmering trees morphing into one. Some incredibly luscious, spacey playing at the very end, with cool patterns from Nick and killer Shon throughout.
Surprisingly deep, intergalactic-aquatic atmosphere, with Brian briefly utilizing a cool, crackling, shimmering effect.
A season-defining jam that loops entrancingly and cyclically through a thick, jungle-like cosmos before instinctively syncing with an active fire alarm.
Slips under radar with impeccable instinct, mimicking the mechanical movements of partially rendered birds and tadpoles as it makes its way up massive obsidian stones toward the sun.
Some insane work from Cory and Brian packed in here.
A Dirtbath-y take on the usual start of the jam gets down quickly and moves through a digital dancehall, grooving perfectly from tile to tile before shifting into Down Under.
A bit of extra energy on this one.
Transcendently floats through lush space in its opening minutes before peaking beautifully.
Cool, static-y, electro undertone.
Mind-meltingly entrancing grooving driven by nearly every patch and synth at Cory’s disposal, peaking nicely with a commanding Brian and consistently strong Shon.
Richly spacey.
A revolving candy store of spacey goodness, capped with a killer ending.
Basks in a pool of translucent gel as it undergoes a full-body scan (not too dissimilar from 1/24/25) before groovily stumbling its way -> ETS.

Flies through rainbow space tunnels, bouncing off vibrant debris before being shot between merging stars and into uncharted territory, where it turns on its High Beams and anxiously builds forward -> Night After Night.
Bubbles nicely.
Similar in scope to Plush jams from Spring/Summer, this one kicks into a higher gear for a rocking, electro-infused final stretch and a fiery ending.
An inverted version that slides into a dialed-in, deeply funky jam that heats up toward a peak before Brian goes all out.
Short and straightforward, but a tremendous sonic presentation.
Dub-y with an explosive finish.

A laser testing ground with a pulsing, glowing backdrop that wheels into ominous space, spinning brightly to a quick peak before sinking into murky waters, the rudder audibly breaking the surface tension as it drifts away.

An exposé on the current style of jamming, moving through groove-oriented pockets, celebratory electronic playing, swarms of electric killer bees, and rhythm & blues that blooms tribalistically in and out of outer space before ramping -> All My Friends.
Super slick final couple of minutes.

song: The Way You Do the Things You Do
notes: Standard first half, followed by a second half that descends into a subaquatic tunnel system, refracting light as it moves toward the beach and morphs into the sunrise.
Two jams with straightforward yet entrancing grooving.
Cycles quickly into a buildup that flashes them into groovy space, where they bounce between walls, toy with the tempo, send out signals, and dive into a beautiful, vibrant pond.
Roams through dissected till plains before grooving down glossy, velvet-projected paths.
Laid back trance.
Jump rope synthpop that slides into nocturnal grooving and heats into an implosive, fantastic ending.

Wobbles funkily through a city before coasting down a desert highway that grows glitzy with grand piano, heating up as it heads toward bright lights. A brief hesitation, then it gears -> Darkness Singularity.

Runs alongside a bright white, raging river before unexpectedly hitting the trail’s end and joining an alien dance ritual, grooving into the night and sneaking past a train as it launches into mutant space disco that robotically rocks its way upward.
Straight reggae that shoots into outer space.
Two jams - the first flutters patiently, the second moves through spacey New Wave before a flashy build.
Smooth, circular funk that grows hot.
Drops into incredible drum and bass.
A triumphant full-band effort with great stuff from everyone, especially Nick. The stretch from 4:14–4:23 alone is some of Cory’s best work ever!
A tight, playful sprinkler of a groove that builds smoothly and surprisingly -> Ain’t That Wrong’s ending.
Easy '80s.
Excellent electropop.
Locked-in drum and bass that drifts into outer space before a customary second half.
Debut. Taps into awesome Afro-Funk.
Fun grooving throughout, with the final couple of minutes featuring beautiful, jazzy playing that grows increasingly anxious.
Infectious, bouncing space disco.
A very well-done Type I jam, with a few minutes of ethereal, electronic grooving at the end.

Jazzy and low-key for the first few minutes before setting sail between icebergs illuminated by aural projections, with sod roof houses and geometric figures moving in looped animations until the energy goes out. Backup generative power kicks in, gradually reloading an underglow of white light through the landscape, eventually going into overdrive and peaking brightly before hitting the main theme, then shifting into a syncopated, plinko disco that gets spacey and drifts between colossal rocks shaped and charred by millions of years of aquatic and volcanic activity.
A dreamscape of assembly line robots working on water toward an explosive finish. -> All My Friends.
Bursts with funk early before making its way through a tunnel toward a classy, future funk-infused city, eventually pulling back to watch its relaxed, glowing skyline set in twilight.
Digital bamboo-garden groove glides past the industrial gearings of a spaceship, lands on a glitzy, jazzy dance-floor of a planet, and gets chased through canyons to a close.
Some great 'hey' jamming in the first five minutes, showcasing fantastic listening and communication from everyone. Lowkey until the final third, where they build to a close.
Upbeat chicken-scratch guitar and bluesy piano, very Dr. John at times. Turns ominous in the final minutes before going -> Walls.

The Postman goes forest mode, swims through a '90s pool commercial, and marches toward a twinkling twilight inlet, overlooking contemplatively before plunging in and skipping into -> Electric Taco Stand.
Spirograph funk blooms into excellent, emotional peaks before easing into reflective, pastoral space -> Diana.
Electro groove takes a scenic trip through intergalactic valleys and mountains, building to a radiant peak before settling into a calm awakening in a bubbling hot spring.
Immersive atmosphere with a groove that builds cleanly.
Hypnotic groove.

Eccentric, upbeat funk sprouts in the final 10 minutes, with wailing guitar surfing above. Lands somewhere between Galisteo Way, All My Friends, and Broken Wing, before an energetic build and smooth slide -> Back in L.A.
Lowkey, spacious ETS-style groove that builds serenely.
Customary funk melts into glowing cave paintings of molten lava.
An initial celebratory drill launches into mechanically circular space, building brightly before swirling into melancholic yet uplifting bluesy territory.
Toys with an Echoes-adjacent groove in the first half before splashing through a Salamander Song stream in the second. -> Salamander Song.
A solid spin on the usual synthpop for the first two thirds, before slipping into an unexpected, slinky groove with Cory teasing Echoes that speeds its way back into -> Duncan's Uncle.
Bounces on water and stays lowkey, with a smooth slide -> Anyone.
A transitive walk through gooey sprinkler showers as dawn breaks across slightly manicured fields, with sprawling guitar and a fierce sunrise.
Nimble to start, patient through the second and final thirds, and emotive throughout.
A glossy, saturated, bouncy groove emerges, riding along until it ramps up cleanly to a close.
Determined playing throughout, with a circular groove and tastes of different spaces thanks to Cory's keys.
Waterfalls and forests glow under sizzling lamps, growing hotter until they burst into radiant flames.
Standard until the last five minutes, where they slowly build their way -> Swingtown.
Upbeat, consistent, and groovy until 13:50, when they drop into a fantastic rave that works its way to a rocket launch transition -> Ain't That Wrong.
Straightforward, but Shon lays down an awesome, steady groove.
Moves through a shimmering, timbered wilderness before dipping its toes into the water, swimming downstream, and eventually fading into night -> High Beams. Absolutely beautiful scenery.
The first opener since 6/11/23 (Press Room, Portsmouth, NH) ending a 190 show gap.

song: The Way You Do the Things You Do
notes: Trudges through gooey (sorta lethargic) space before moving onto a dazzling dancefloor. A round of peaks, and then a choppy groove that builds brightly -> Back in L.A.
A bit out of the box, with some slowdowns, and samples.
Dub-y and Funkadelic-y to start, slowing at a space terminal before swirling into a dancey strait with a fiery finish.
Straightforward first half that flies by, then Funkadelic-ish jamming that experiments with several combinations before opening up into an 8-bit groove that eventually swings -> Walls.
Mostly the usual structure, but much spacier.
Hustles in double time before hitting a section straight from Windmill, then quickly moves through a corridor of buzzing lights and into a dense, foggy jungle -> Broken Wing.
A revolving carousel of a groove that builds sharply and reflects brightly.
Rushes into a funky, mechanical marshland, where it churns until the peak.

The roof opens to an Arctic forest doused in constellations that steadily scorches its way back to the main theme. From there, it becomes a mid-morning drive through the countryside, rolling onto  and around a nocturnal, deeply colorful electric dancefloor by highway studded with floating crystals. It grows ominous, features a phone-call sample, and goes -> Can't Catch Me Now.
Transparent blocks and containers of light drop and neatly sort themselves above the countryside.
Awesome keys, samples, and time changes in the first few minutes. A bit of icing on the cake for Chuck's birthday.
Brighter than usual, with a robotic entity happily sending out signals and painting the universe with its blazing trail.
Spends its final minutes building serenely -> Anyone.

Strobes scatteredly before touring the inner workings of an open-air ship, surfacing to a Monaco coastline dazzling with nightlife and riddled with traffic, then builds brightly into a radiant sunrise.
Swirls into outer space, swims for a bit, and then explodes into a star.
Stomps its way into a disco at Shon's insistence, slowly building before a quick implosion -> Space Gadget.
A swampy, funky groove emerges and sticks until spacey, windchime-y keys appear, swooning to the edge of the atmosphere, where things slowly get angry and go -> Dis Go In 5?
Briefly calms down into a peaceful garden inside of a spaceship before building -> Who Can It Be Now?
Shiny, regenerative groove that catches storm warnings and takes shelter in a funky basement.

Keeps the swampy theme alive with Shon's colorful green and brown tones, then swirls underwater to swim through a parallel outer space, revolving around a sun before and during an eclipse, rotating steadily -> Ain't That Wrong.
Calms down into a soulful, minimalistic scene that drifts -> Palisades.
Pokes and prods in the dark before briefly stumbling on a celestial celebration, then slips into customary electro-rock and drifts into serene, tribal-tinged waters that go -> The Other One.
Straightforward, but bright throughout and done well.

A soundstage of an early 1980s Caribbean dancehall that pulses circuitously through the night until a distant early warning is heard and it responds with sharper pace and direction. Absolutely fantastic work and determination from everyone, especially Brian.
Snappier than usual and outside the box, with some nice space.
Floats into outer space and attaches to a repetitive, entrancing groove for a good while until Cory steps up with organ and they start to work towards a peak.

Triggered consecutive implosions to carve artificial canyons on the crest of the city, letting shades of light surface. A nighttime flyover leads to a clash between auroras and city lights, building to a monstrous peak that settles down, slyly boogies, and incredibly rocks its way -> Night After Night.
Grooves dreamily for its first half before being searched for by an intergalactic yeti and its planetary spotlight, eventually reaching a gloomy waterside that brightens to a close.
Slinks its way around a pond garden with a heavy presence. Great stuff from Brian throughout.

Some unusual rave-y vocal samples pop up after a few minutes, swirling out of thick clouds and hovering over a duplitecture of a city, sensing glowing architectural patterns mapped out by Shon's bass and streets of glossy, running streams that Cory paves. It speeds up quickly and closes out perfectly. Look out!
Bobs steadily with a low-key groove for a good bit.
Straightforward, but peaks nicely and has some bluesy playing at the end that drops into Cantaloupe Island.
Super smooth, with a soulful solo from Brian.

A rainbow's take on the "second story basement in an underwater matrix" to start, with vibrant colors from everyone and a speedy pace on display. It cools down in the final third, coasting somewhere between Careful With That Axe, Eugene and Breakdown (Petty), before building -> Motel 6.
Drifts out to sea and onto a cloud where it bathes in misty, monochromatic green air.
Bounces for a bit before sliding into a familiar intergalactic rave that builds angrily -> Virtual Bean Dip.
Extra synth goodness with poised playing throughout.
Basically Night After Night for the first half, then swims downstream into patient, soulful playing and slides off a waterfall -> Windmill.
Upbeat funk that that slowly turns straight boogie, moves through emotional early-2000s electro and lands softly.
Sharp synthpop slides into a chill, arid garden and climbs to a peak.
Quickly latches onto a syncopated groove and makes its way to feel-good, Summer-time territory.
Upbeat and locked in from the start, then meanders through vocal sample territory before finding its footing on a rumbling, determined groove.
Serene, free-flowing jamming in the first half that swings into clean peaks. Some Funkadelic-ish grooving in the last 10 minutes that slides outside to a nature preserve and -> The Postman.
Stutter-step funk with a repetitive grand piano that builds brightly. Killer Brian in the final third.
Funky, flower-garden groove melts in place with loops swirling overhead before warming up and dancing down the Soul Train Line.
First appearance since 12/31/19 (San Francisco, CA), ending a 408 show gap. Lots of samples from Cory.
An earworm of a groove that pedals mechanically, with a soaring, atmospheric background that teases its way to a beautiful buildup. Like the sun peeking out from clouds.
Summertime groove turns electronically somber. -> Aliens.
Mechanical showering in a rainbow-glowing jungle at night.
Slinks its way to a beautiful buildup and lands on a double time groove for the last few minutes.
Upbeat and funky, moving through 1980s streets before building anxiously. Gets quiet for a minute, then grooves cleanly into -> Anyone.
More intense than usual to start and determined throughout.
Standard groove turns dancey before Cory slides and hammers on the grand piano. Ramps up and drops cleanly -> Can't Find My Vape.

Wobbly funk swirls into a shimmering swamp of spacey synths and poppy beats, then Brian takes over for an early-2000s groove that swells and drops into brief space before a celestial, celebratory close.
A streaky, funky groove gets concentrated and almost robotic. Cool stuff from Cory and Shon throughout.
The first jammed version. Toys with a playful groove.
Plucky, windchime-y keys from Cory over a sprinkler-patterned, ska-tinted groove, with a powerful final third.
Patient funk that churns slowly for a while and works its way to -> The Postman.
Dub-y for a bit and builds intently.

Funky with a distinct Echoes-like sound for the first few minutes that shifts to super groovy, Shon-driven space where they sway as a unit before hitting the peak. Some colorful playing that in the last minute or so that fades > Dissociation Assist.
Swirls into a heavy, trancey groove that builds sharply before a rocking close.
Slinky, slow groove with some awesome Shon that grows angry.
Starts out with some surprising jump blues and gets weirder before hitting an early peak that Brian crushes. Some extra, hoppy, Funkadelic-ish jamming in the back third.
Hang gliding over indoor oceans and starlit shores. -> Walls.
Standard, but done well. Nice buildup -> Broken Wing.
Bouncy, groovy, and picks up speed half way through for a 1970s progressive rock buildup and peak.
Instantly latches to a P-Funk groove that Shon gets turned way up for. One of the best buildups ever here.
Early Electro House, with some crazy stuff from Brian towards the end.
Heated playing from Brian on display.

A cyclical disco by nature, one that progresses patiently and consistently. Its groove morphs subtly and funkily, building to a soaring peak that Brian explodes over, and finishes with a twilight-tinted slide -> War of Man.
Steadily up-tempo and sticking with a danceable groove that just won't quit, this one anxiously works its way up a cliff that abruptly drops off into -> Alternate Ending.

Drifts into a simulated rice field under a projection of a blue sky, as gigantic intergalactic beasts of vehicles stroll into the scene, tearing the fabric of the projected sky and leaving behind a wide, shining rainbow that speeds up time before straightening out for a celebratory build back into ETS.

Glides and rewinds in stuttering motion down a mountainside blanketed with snow, gaining speed as it robotically dodges rocks, branches, and terrain as if it were on rails before slipping into a deep hibernation dimly lit by swirling colors and muted hues. From there, it takes its time to wake up with neat, bluesy playing that turns bright and reels into several minutes of ETS teasing that, you guessed it, goes -> ETS.

Cory slides in with some synths around the 7:00 mark, hits the echo 45 seconds later, then wipes them into atmospheric, funky, rumbling space that he and Shon control for most of the jam. Last few minutes has a powerful Brian on display. More than a few "this is the first set!?" moments here.
Rotates funkily for its first half, hits a clean buildup, then waltzes through slick, jazzy territory that bobs steadily and implodes to the ending.
Upbeat and fun, shifting through busy lanes with poise and a determined pace before shooting out of the city and then the atmosphere.
An Ibizan rainforest speckled with spry, swirling stars that industrializes toward a customary peaking section.

Quickly drops into a smoke-filled underwater Matrix in a second story basement and breaks out to fiercely bright skies before finding its way to a slinking, Echoes-y groove that fades and goes -> Double Time.
Has an easygoing, Summer-time groove. The shortest version of the year (?)
Locks in on a consonant groove that Cory works his magic over for the first half before Brian unleashes for the second half. Some really good Shon here.
Starts out with an Anyone-esque groove, brightens, finds itself on a gothic dancefloor of sorts, and goes -> Walls.
A late-night, mid-century modern drive with a nice groove to it that swells with electric nervousness and descends into smoother space to > In the Eyes of Thieves. Fantastic.
Bookending a Walls -> Made for Wesley -> Walls sandwich, this one utilizes a familiar groove and features a scorching last few minutes where Brian steals the show.
Quickly drops into a cosmic aquarium tunnel that reaches surprising depth and gets trippy. -> Made for Wesley.
Some Spring-time sounds from Cory throughout and a nice groove that quickens and brightens to the end.
Drifts along a Longview-like beachside and into spacious, warm water that rolls to a peak. Great stuff from Brian towards the end.
Instantly hits a funky groove, quickly gives way to a vocal jam, and returns for some awesome P-Funk that moves through a mechanical checkpoint and drifts slightly out of orbit.
A feel-good vibe that bobbles steadily for a good bit, then floats along shimmering, saturated, heavy water -> Night After Night.
Lush in parts and progresses nicely.
Supremely funky and up-tempo, this one swirls into an Anatolian suite and breaks out with power.

Funky through the first half and propels into a spacey rave with a very strong Shon and steady Nick. Brian takes over in the last few minutes for some great emotive playing. The start of a ETS > Dis Go In 5? > ETS sandwich.
Starts out with a mechanical groove, gains traction and soars with a contemplative Cory behind it, then glides through sunset lava lamp constellations -> Electric Taco Stand.
Extended electro house with a few big buildups.
Features Tim Palmieri on guitar and starts with some synthpop, turns electronic, and swirls into sharper cat-and-mouse between Brian and Tim. Clean slide into the ending.
Settles on anticipated funk before building to an early 2000s Electro close.
Unreal Tournament 1999 x Rainbow Road x Star Wars Episode I Racer. (Colorful drum and bass turns jazzy, shifts to funkier space, and exits with power -> Neutrino.)
An entrancing Latin jazz rave that slides into a concentrated groove that Cory dances over with several keyboards before settling on the grand piano.
Lethargic through much of the first half, but swirls into a Miami nightclub around 9:00, peaks soulfully with a twinkling comedown, and has a feel-good roots rock build -> Mind's Unchained.
Short, but doesn't feel like it. A tiny bit atmospheric to start the jam and a strong, blues-y Southern Rock second half.
Mostly standard, but goes double time for a minute or so towards the end.
Awesome groove with standout Shon that gets a bit evil at times. Awkward first step into Broken Wing, but smooths out for the transition.
Starts out slow and funky, with some sample manipulation from Cory before going breakbeat. Gets spacey in the middle.
Stutter-step funk with a brief electro phase.

PlayStation 1 nostalgia ambient atmospheric jungle drum and bass mix.



(Truly inspired, up-tempo drum and bass. Easily one of the best versions this year.)
A whirring, Afro-Funk solo from Cory and tight throughout.
Feat. Rob Compa on guitar. Starts out with a metronomic groove before turning spacey and dancey. Some cool sheets of sonic rain from Cory launch them into a rocket-race between Brian and Rob.
A slick, saturated groove sprouts with the help of ever-consistent Shon, loops hanging overhead before building with bite. Some delicate, serene playing stumbles into another lowkey groove to close.
Funky with some sharp synths and a screeching close.
An open-air train ride through mountains just before dawn, with a sprawling sunrise.
Awesome, engaging, up-beat Electro-Disco that slips out of orbit, climbs into a sunspot, and bursts with color. Ferocious.

One of those "this one's going to be different" moments as they slide into the jam. Starting with a funkier base than usual, it moves through polished synthpop, a brief but stunning atmospheric passage, more funk, and has some great guitar work from Brian at the end.
Ice skating on a haptic rainbow Alp during a solar eclipse.
Ethereal atmosphere blooms into a steady groove that peaks around 20:00, then goes back into atmospheric space before turning celebratory to close.
Relaxed groove that turns spacey and boards a midnight sky train with shimmering lights and shapes below. Big sunrise build > Todd's Tots.

A determined groove pops up instantly, diving into an underwater matrix in a second story basement that opens into a rave. Huge buildup around 12:00, followed by fluttery, feel good playing that bursts with pride > Salamander Song.
Just the fifth ever show opener and a good one at that, steadily marching its way into a playful groove that Cory lays synths on top of. Nice build and fade -> Fake the Fate.
A signature Spafford groove develops and wipes into repetitive, patient space for several minutes. Snare hit at 12:35 and they're off to another mini-buildup and drop.

Locks onto an entrancing groove that gets down early and delivers an awesome first 15 minutes. A few meandering moments thereafter, but they swing colorfully into another hard-hitting groove and hit peaks before closing out. Great.
Ethereal with ambient swells for a good few minutes before some midi/mutron playing from Brian that flows neatly to peaks.
Around 12:00, beams of synths begin to soar through a pristine summer Arctic landscape before  driving into a nocturnal Northern European city with a steady groove -> In the Eyes of Thieves.
Smoothly slides from a rainy, tropical purple backyard into a churning late-night intergalactic disco, with some face-melting shredding from Brian and nice playing from Cory before closing out.
Just the fifth show opener to date, this one gets excited early and spends its first 17 minutes brightly building to an explosive peak. Final third features some blues-y playing -> Ice Cream.
Ska turns into an airy, nighttime groove -> Down Under.

Races through an intergalactic jungle war zone on an up-tempo, cyclical groove that weaves around monorails and hovering structures, with an electrical grid glowing beneath in volcanic yellows and oranges. Killer throughout, with a very clean slide to close.
Debut. Colorfully funky and deliciously electronic.
Fluttery and intricate first half.
Meditative groove that's easy to get lost in.
Extra juice, with some hard-hitting, emotional guitar work.
A groove straight from Off the Wall (Michael Jackson) that soars through space and peaks nicely.
A tale of two halves: first, Frogger in a dense, metallic-green jungle where nothing feels real; then, a steady groove sprouts from the main theme and builds with pace and energy -> Motel 6.
Consistent rave that flutters into Palisades.
Celebratory, with an incredible Brian.

A Duncan's Uncle-esque groove that drifts through vocal pad trance, hits a sharp peak, and circles back with a low-key take on the earlier groove before building (impressively!) to -> Night After Night.
Settles on a relaxed, thumping groove driven by Shon and has a chaotic, slightly jazzy buildup.
Goes double time and moves into colorful, iridescent electro before peaking with power.

Goes through deep funk before sliding into an awesome, glacial landscape that runs through a couple of powerful yet somber peaks before filtering out. Some killer Brian here, and a great, loud full-band sound.
Bounces on pristine, colorful tiles soaked in sunlight, exerting immense energy in what seems an impossible attempt to reach the top, and gets rewarded with the view of a lifetime.

Breaks out from the quiet part (the quiet part!) into spectacular, electronically dyed, entrancing space that grows eclectically and powers its way back into the second half of the song proper. Everything you've ever wanted.
Spacey, loopy, and showcases several different time signatures and new electronics.
The usual deal (but done very well) for the first half, then gets funky and works its way toward a peak straight out of Salamander Song, before slamming into Salamander Song itself.

An open-air amphitheater tucked in patches of thick, lush grass within a city, framed by buildings looming overhead as stutter-step funk echoes through the park until the sun sets, when things get atmospheric and peak with the moon's rise.
Sunbathes in a springtime mountainous stream.

Swirls into deep space, finding it self in a jazzy strait of miniature planets before descending to an angular alleyway, guided by flares pointing to a massive, nondescript facility buried deep within an industrialized city. Inside lies a limestone cave studded with stalactites and subwoofers, housing a mechanical rave and opening onto an enormous quartz block where purple lights strobe and shadows skip against perfectly placed pillars until the scene zooms out to a galactic tea garden.
Bounces into vast outer space for the first half and travels through an unexpectedly happy cycle in the second, with a bright, satisfying peak and a calm end.

Instantly gets incredibly airy and spacious, like swaths of grass swaying in the wind chiming softly, before growing electronic and drifting into an outer-space lullaby that rocks and revolves around a glitzy disco ball.
Bobs into an entrancing rave.
Powerful!

Gets neuralyzed and transported into the doorway of an intergalactic hallway, one end opening onto a busy railway of imperfectly rendered trains, each looping and weaving in random animations. Sound bounces from a second story basement nearby as a heat signature alert leads to a chase and big peak -> Alternate Ending.
A noticeably strong start that makes its way into a geodesic sphere containing millions of galaxies, radiating in transcendent shapes and forms of different colors and intensities.
Perfect, celebratory playing from everyone and a superb remaster featured on the Flight of Fall '25 compilation.
Spacey to start and incredibly tight throughout.
Washes into rich, shimmering space where it floats tranquilly before shooting back through the atmosphere to reach the main theme. Fantastic.
Incredibly strong, with tight playing from everyone, a celebratory jam, and a beautiful, hard-hitting final couple of minutes.
Coming round from an exceptional Anyone, this one sways patiently for a couple of minutes before going straight into its ending. OHHHHHHHHHHH!
An easy-to-digest groove that blooms around the 15-minute mark before descending into an abandoned lakeside amphitheater.
Cool throughout, with an extra buildup, too. Really slick.

An ear-ringing call from outer space leads to a trip in a hopping space rover, bright light dyeing its metallic body in assorted washed-out colors as its climbs through rocky terrain, hits a major peak with a triple moonrise, then calms down and builds -> Night After Night.

Ziplines into a world filled with translucent pink and purple blobs of jelly breathing as random units, then builds into a travelator within an infinite pattern of gold and steel pyramids that snap and unfold into and onto each other. The second jam features a funky groove that grows spacious and joyful.
Surfaces to an underwater strip of rainbow belts, where it cruises and bounces signals back and forth until it peaks sharply and calms considerably.
An exceptional run through with a repetitive groove that spins electrically, grows mechanically, and explodes with incredible force.

Looks for ghosts in and along industrial piping before driving down a dusty highway at sunset, the frame of the vehicle melting away until night falls, when a thick fog surrounds them and transports them into deep space, where they drift for a bit before gearing back up with a funky groove that eventually winds down.

Woodpecking into liquid glass shatters the universe into goo, building to a monstrous peak that Brian slays. From there, it relaxes into a northern seaside park, misty breeze running through, where angelic visions briefly appear before giving way to a tribal buildup -> Dirtbath.
This one's a rager!

song: Shu Ba Da Du Ma Ma Ma Ma
notes: Micro-jam packed with peaks.
Very colorful electro that widens into space and goes -> Legend of Zelda.

A quick Hood jam (in reference to the previous night's "I said when we 'knew' how to play that, not 'know'" banter) that slow-drips across a simulated Moab desert, surveils for extraterrestrial life, then explodes into the sun and dissipates.
Standard funk quiets, then builds into atmospheric, mechanical disco dream pop that peaks fantastically and has a cool outro -> Soggy Froggy.
A much happier take on the usual deal.
Shakes into a late night drive lit by striving lights and echoing sounds.
Slick grooving morphs into vibrant electro that grows hot and hits hard.
Dreams into a dark box with a window looking out to a small coastline and an endless ocean, while the sunrise gradually fills the room with refracted colors.
Devastatingly good final minute or so.
Afro-funk space invasion.

Jam starts at the midway point of the song and sprouts like a universe from a lone, halfway-planted seed, adorned with silk waterfalls that bend and mist minimalistic drumming as they rotate through space, setting course for an exploding star where they peak spectacularly.

White hot playing from Brian between verses and a light, bouncy start to the jam that grows groovy as it dips its toes in a stream, electrifying the surrounding area to the maximum. Then they skip into deep space, working their way into a guarded, semi-industrialized village that raves away.

"Shon... funkdalelic? Spun... kadelic? Ska punk-adelic. OH, it's sped up!" 



Colorful, mechanical space disco that races from start to finish.

song: The Way You Do the Things You Do
notes: Wharf Rat-y and Dark Star-ish, peaking fiercely before snapping into a power-building groove that grows chaotic.

Moves into a strobing, vibrant disco framed by comforting, blinking, and twirling lights that grows radiant and triumphant until it peaks with the main theme. The second jam begins with a hard-hitting, Funkadelic-style groove before giving way to a soundscape of glacial streams flowing through rock formations that lead to an alien ceremony, followed by streaky guitar and a buildup straight out of Darkness Singularity.
Two jams, both of which show off a lot of new sounds but ultimately make for straightforward jamtronica.

A looser start to the jam than usual, with playful Off the Wall / Wanna Be Startin’ Somethin’ teasing before stepping into a shower of vibrating meteors whose particles dash and shift positions with sharp color, making for a big buildup and a spacey exit.
Piercing, soulful guitar playing throughout.
Aliens-esque, noisy deep space.
Cool, colorful grooving, but a bit same-y in spots.
Dissipates into a hazy, misty coastal highway before gearing into a Double Time-y buildup.
Sails into a spacey, joyful, and repetitive groove before marching away.
Really well done Type I jam.

Lowered into an Arctic race at the peak of a solar eclipse, this one moves blindly through an infinite landscape, waving at holograms of competitors from decades past until the sun strikes just right and shatters their vision into greyscale, with flashes of orange in their peripheral vision that burst into raging flames, and has a somber revisit years later.
Swanky, funky grooving that gradually speeds up as it gets spacier, dazzling its way toward -> Can't Find My Vape with an awesome transition.
One of Brian's guitar strings uncoils, prompting some fun improv from the other three before he returns to demolish with an explosive finish.
Lots of different keys from Cory, with a cool yacht rock jam that builds cleanly.
Back and forth alien chatter.
Colorful, splatter paint groove that builds with an All My Friends-y sound.
Standard, soaring grooving that drops into sparse space before building -> Walls.

song: I Wouldn't Want to Be Like You
notes: Slightly slower than usual, with some super slick organ.

Hazy, ambient atmosphere backing a grand piano solo morphs into an Ibizan sprinkler of a groove that projects swaying, closed-eye jump rope visuals on rotating walls and shapes before it hits the main theme.
Consistently fun grooving throughout.
Entrancing, semi-aquatic grooving with some impressive guitar work from Brian.
Rolls into a Mu-Tron-laden stream that bubbles with an electronic shimmer before blooming into a huge peak.
Pendulum funk that briefly derails before catching another groove and bursting into a major peak, finishing out with a few minutes of Echoes-y playing that gets fiery.
The usual rave with swirling lights overhead takes a turn into bright territory, peaks nicely, then flutters into a buildup toward -> Galisteo Way.
An incredibly spirited and impressive run through the song itself leads to a determined, celebratory jam that settles into a funky groove before eventually dropping away.
Hard-hitting electro calms into an alien campfire before circling back to close.
A blast to the past (Summer... three months ago) for a very summery, 80s jam that implodes powerfully.
Entrancing, repetitive grooving with a fantastic buildup and peak.
Really dialed in version with an explosive finish, which completes the first Froggy -> Frog combination (ha!).
Big-time boogying stutters into a mechanical, bumping groove that moves back and forth like water before dipping into a Mu-Tron sparked, swooping buildup.
Beams reflect and duplicate between a room of mirrors.

The first jam gradually and beautifully builds to some tasteful shredding from Brian, while the second moves into playful New Wave bopping before sinking into a calm bay, with drivers’ lights oscillating and reflecting off the water, as driving etiquette instructions float them into -> High Beams.

Phases through futuristic bacterial force fields into an energetic, bluesy, Broken Wing-esque jam that spreads into a fun, saturated, blocky groove before submerging into a vibrant jungle that progresses nicely, builds to a beautiful peak, and slips out of orbit.
A determined rave with killer playing from Cory that doubles down on the electronics, working in new sampled quotes and a fast, echoing groove that boomerangs around rotating sirens.
Cool grooving that sprouts rich funk, a big peak, and a spacey last couple of minutes. Check out 4/17/25 for a very similar jam that takes things to the next level.
Super spacey, with lots of cool sounds.
Nice, swingy jam that rocks to a satisfying close.
Short, but solid playing quickly tumbles headfirst into a huge buildup, erupting into an absolutely fire earworm of a groove.
Flowing in from Shelter in Place, this closes out the Broken Wing sandwich with booming bass from Shon, a dose of heavy funk, and a clean slide away -> Shu Ba Da Du Ma Ma Ma Ma.
Piercing, expressive playing from Brian melts into a Venusian hot spring that raves softly.
Moves through a beaded curtain into a thriving, colorful simulation, building cleanly and peaking with polish.
Loud and mechanical. Very cool in certain spots.
Swirls into unexpected funky, Echoes-y jamming that swings smoothly -> Shelter in Place.

Another impeccable run through the song proper, with the customary first jam calming considerably before building back with a funky groove that peaks brightly and flows directly into Broken Wing's ending.
Moves down a semi-industrial road at night, with cars passing infrequently until it notices it's being followed, leading to a high-speed chase and a major peak.
A solid run through, with the electronics sounding more dialed in with each outing.
Patient playing gradually brightens with soaring exposure and a satisfying peak.
Dances in sync with millions of colorful particles before bursting and working its way -> Mind's Unchained.
Gets slightly tribal in its final minute before Cory hops on saxophone and they head -> Imperial March.
Hazy, glowing background ambiance swirls into an earworm groove that Cory dominates before Brian takes over for a scorching peak.
A very well-executed take on the newer style of jamming, building into a massive ending.
Breezy, slightly angular playing that accelerates at its tail end.
Pastoral, Musette-y playing (at times) builds into an impactful ending.
Shifts into suit before wearily traversing through a wrecked ship filled with electronically pixelated flora and fauna, floating into old-time swing before rocking to a major peak.
Slippery synths give way to a hopping, Plinko-y jam that bounces across layers before settling into a thumping, industrial groove that opens up into a domed rave and rocks back to the main theme.
Awesomely consistent, deep grooving that touches on a couple of different patterns, including some really funky dungeon synth before exploding and sinking.
Colorful, sprinkler-head of a groove.
Sprouts brightly in a patient fashion.
Moves back and forth like water within a neurological maze.
Sunbathes in a field of sunflowers and delphiniums.
Really on-point version with some wackier sounds and samples than usual.
Absolutely locked-in, bumping groove.
Straightforward, solid groove.

Bibbles with opaque shades of vibrant colors before dipping into a matrix inside of a second-story basement, with trails of electricity leaving glowing traces behind as it builds and peaks fiercely, then drops into swingy territory that barrels straight into -> Armageddon.
Ambient techno that grows saturated and builds emotionally -> Legend of Zelda.
About as good as Type I gets.

Images of an intergalactic detection gang on TRAPPIST-1e rolling up to a nondescript landscape and using spectral imaging and radioscopic surveys to scan for signs of life until they penetrate the surface and a massive translucent animatronic whale breaches upward, transforming the terrain into a cosmic ocean of fluttering matrices that float their way toward the shoreline and -> Salamander Song.
Pendulums of oceans swinging and colliding before merging into a dancey, smooth, nu-jazz groove that blooms into -> Spunkadelic.
Supremely funky work with a customary ending.
Ambient swells give way to slick funk that turns into hard boogie with a big ending.
Earworm groove that slinks and bounces across immense cubes of plasmagel.
Awesomely funky throughout, with a grand, bright final third and killer playing from everyone, especially Brian.
Ship XTAR-93’s yearly training exercise takes a trip through the cosmos, glides through a glossy cityscape, and sinks into a dense aquarium.
Great run-through of the song proper.
Drops into an infinite tide pool where crystal-feathered birds dive for cubes of jelly quartz.
Wildly psychedelic.
Opens into a wheat field swaying as another planet drifts into orbit.
Flutters through frontier tunnels and slides into a radioactive wilderness where flora glows purple and interconnected roots of sentience send data back and forth.
A dense, swampy groove emerges and eventually barrels its way into a buildup straight out of Armageddon.

The zap of a television switching off floats them into a sky filled with millions of dancing stars, forming an encompassing layer around their body that glows as they drift past galaxies before being swallowed by the sun.
Groovy and entrancing, but kinda same-y until the last couple of minutes, when it really kicks in and stabs into -> Ain't That Wrong.
Exceptional piano work and a screeching guitar solo.
Insanely funky, Type 1 jam.
Jazzy beginnings lead to slick boogieing that swirls through a syrupy, slightly emotional electro-disco before peaking and settling into somber space.
Deep-space exploration with washes of trillions of galaxies.
A symphonic rave that breathes and builds naturally before galloping away.

song: Shu Ba Da Du Ma Ma Ma Ma
notes: Shon takes a long bass solo, then Cory and Brian link up for a powerful second half.
Super slick funk that rocks its way to a close.
Beautiful!
Sophisticatedly electronic.
Rides the main theme with groovy and rock-y takes for a good while before building patiently into Anyone in the final third.

Bounces into an incredibly colorful, sophisticated network of colossal hands stacking, sliding, and rerouting subway cars filled with millions of people, then zooms in on a single seat, flying past planetary mines hollowing entire worlds from the inside out before slipping into -> Mad World.
Ruffles the spacescape and peeks out from behind an invisible curtain before being labeled as a Space Gadget(!) and rocketing toward Earth.
Some watery back and forth funk on display.

A poised, if not perfect run-through of the song proper, adorned with organ and exquisitely placed grand piano that swings into heavy, dense, colorful grooving that ignites an underwater Latin excursion into a rocket launch.
Seamlessly slides into brilliant chordal jazz with excellent grand piano work and sharply electric guitar.
The blare of horns on a galactic highway leads to unusually bright jamming that flows into Tequila.
Molten hot, scorching playing from Brian and a powerful full-band display.
Soulful, with some piercing guitar.
A truly powerful outing.
Winamp visualizer–style groove that pulses and swirls.
Glossy, polished sophisti-pop.
Funky jump rope builds unexpectedly quickly and blooms into a progressively electronic flower that pollinates a city before bursting and breathing slowly into Anyone.
Power Pop ending!
Flow-state grooving.
Exceptional, full-band, locked-in grooving with a heated ending.
Similar to recent outings, but hits a fantastic Afro-electronic patch in its final minutes.
Finds itself drifting into space with a relaxed, lo-fi beat directed by Nick before phasing into beautiful plunderphonics in its final couple of minutes.
Features a quick, unusually angry and noisy build.
Rolls into the flavor of the month before detonating into a massive buildup and electric trance.

Feat. Mike Savino on banjo. Back-and-forth “getting our feet wet” playing between Brian and Mike turns into a solar expedition that peaks feverishly before getting knocked off course into a funky strait of stars. From there, things go dark as they prod deeper, eventually imploding -> Motel 6.

Feat. Mike Savino on banjo. Incredible new synth patches pop up within the song itself and radiate into a shimmering, futuristic electroacoustic jam that builds to a massive, triumphant ending before turning back to the song’s second half.

An impressive outing for the song itself, framed by an immense early peak, energetic drumming from Nick, and unbelievable playing from Brian. From there, it moves through a refined take on the current - yet ever-evolving - style of jamming with pace and poise before erupting volcanically and building towards The Other One.
Ending only. Builds angrily and energetically to finish out the year.
Stunning downtempo.
Scans through thick clouds for crystalline biosignatures before flying into the dark and -> Weasel.
Sequenced synth phases in a loop as Cory jumps on saxophone, rotating through entrancing Afrobeat.
Absurdly colorful funk that repeatedly builds into higher levels of the dance floor before dissipating into hazy noise.
Circular, robotic stomping.
Aesthetically similar to 1/17/25 Ain’t That Wrong, this one takes a laid-back approach as it moves through and along a city’s port.
Unbelievably funky jamming that slides around funk sirens(!) and new vocal samples before detaching from the vessel and swimming through repetitive, murky waves.
One jam, driven by Cory across a couple of different synths, with a surprisingly funky patch woven in.

Sprouts into robust synthpop where stars dance in radial patterns before flowering electronically and triumphantly into a massive peak. Several stars converge and explode, dousing the universe in hot light that tears into a futuristic, tropical subway before drifting into deeply spacious downtempo to assess the damage from millions of light-years before. Emotional, soaring guitar carries them through fiery canyons before thumping toward a bright, dancey buildup that dreams itself back into beautiful, soulful space, building back into The Other One proper. Extraordinary.
Bounces into ethereal space before peaking nicely.
Brighter jamming than usual with incredible tension and release and a massive peak that circles back to the main theme, making for an excellent first 11 minutes.
Sparkles electronically before building toward a fierce electro-rock second half.
Full-band teases of Soggy Froggy lead to low-key grooving that grows molten hot.
Loud, raging funk with sharp guitars and a  dancing backdrop. Killer!
Beautiful final couple of minutes!
Groovy and builds steadily.
A beautiful opening featuring emotional grand piano work gives way to an absurdly funky jam with several distinct layers.
Celebratory and energetic to the max.
Flies between electronically blinking Afro-Funk stars as Cory cycles through several different keys.
Unexpected Post-Punk grooving on the main theme pops up and slows before morphing -> Mad World.
Drifts across intergalactic highways before speeding toward a close.
Hardcore funk morphs into a revolving dreamscape that heats up to a fiery finish.
Wades through radiant downtempo for a good stretch before catching a train that speeds across open plains -> Motel 6.
Shuffles across a foggy highway at the edge of the atmosphere, with indistinct vehicles sliding by and disappearing, before trekking down into a bubbling, electronic ravine that explodes.
Chimes into beautiful synthpop, driven by a thumping Shon and steady Brian, before surging into an immense peaking section.
Speeds through its first half before settling into a groovy second that grows saturated.
Boogies intently through outer space before revving through waves of electronic storms, firing straight into the sun and then calming into emotional space.
Well done, straightforward jam that peaks powerfully before settling into some grooving on Echoes.

song: Shu Ba Da Du Ma Ma Ma Ma
notes: Terse, with a great build.
Swirls into a booming, repetitive, outrageously funky groove that Brian goes scorched-earth in the second half for.
Electronic tingling and vibrations.
Starts with grooving on Gotta Jibboo before sliding into colorful, entrancing space that peaks quickly and powerfully.
An upbeat outing with face melting playing throughout.
A patient, beautiful, borderline transcendent first jam that steadily climbs toward a mountainous peak.
Consistently sharp playing builds into beautiful synthpop, peaking brilliantly with the main theme before rolling into a second, funky jam that features tons of good ideas from Shon.
Twangs through the countryside before catching an unusually funky wave, hitting a slick nu-jazz buildup, and sliding masterfully back into the main theme.
Encompassing, textural house glides through space before thumping into a trance.
Almost Night After Night-ish in its initial approach, this one grooves along an intergalactic coastline before heading -> Anyone (no peak!).
An unusual, stripped-down Afro-funk breakdown opens the jam, unfurling into slick, churning grooving before bopping its way into celebratory space.
A great Type 1 outing that really heats up in the second half for a raging peak.

Tasteful, moving through quieter space before engaging with an all-in mindset and marching toward a peak that reveals beautiful scenery, then repeating the cycle all over again for an exquisite, larger-than-life final peak. Outstanding.

A quick intro gives way to green, easygoing territory where Nick and Shon link up for a sprinkler groove that sprays colorful walkways Brian dances down, with Cory in tow, connecting deep space to Afro-Cuban-infused waters. From there, Brian takes the reins for an incredibly celebratory, soulful passage that teeters on the edge of Fuego before veering back to the main theme to close out the first jam. The second jam takes a straightforward, funky route, making for a somewhat lackluster ten or so minutes before an impressive, patient, orchestral build -> Todd’s Tots.
Features an extensive, cold, 1980s sci-fi intro.
Expressive, inspired, molten playing from Brian drives the first half, followed by an unusual, patient, emotive, spacious jam that gets out there before bridging back gracefully to a close.
Straightforward, but does feature some High Beams samples and a really heated ending.

Takes off onto a coastal Florida highway, snarling with pace before a quick detour through the swampy South and then bouncing into low orbit, where it hovers over a diorama of the region in a future funk disco that quickly blossoms into beautiful synthpop. It drifts into a murky, spacious groove from there, going into autopilot as it sinks into a regenerative bath, slipping in and out of consciousness until it crash-lands -> America.
More of the usual stuff (though done very well), with some ethereal space tacked on at the tail end.
Drifts out to sea aboard a translucent ship, its lights blinking in the distance until darkness swallows it and the water takes on a psychedelic shimmer. Big ending here, too.
Vibrant, psychedelic, borderline New Jack Swing grooving that gnashes its way to an electric ending.
Stutters into a 20th-century Mid-Atlantic club scene for a good few minutes.
Feat. Kanika Moore on lead vocals. Takes on a shape similar to recent Neutrinos and delivers a great peaking section.
Bathes in beautiful, relaxing downtempo before peaking nicely and shifting into noisy space -> Money for Nothing.

A truly beautiful, multifaceted jam that shoots out of the gate with Crosseyed and Painless teasing and insistent, upbeat grooving before shifting into a mirrored dimension where radar signals bounce off one another, eventually settling into spacious, fluttering waters where it builds nicely before abruptly flipping -> Tainted Love.
Crosseyed and Painless-adjacent jamming opens into groovy space, growing more upbeat as they work their way up a new wave–y coast and getting gritty before sliding -> Spunkadelic (ending only).
Swirls into patient, dreamy space where it wades for a good while before peaking.

Another fantastic, hard-hitting outing for the song itself (with a shoegaze-y, post-grunge-y twinge to it at times), which helps cement this tune as one of their most evocative at the moment. Practically no “pursuit,” just instantly gratifying trance that phases through electronic bubbles before brightening for a massive peak and then drawing the curtains closed for a bluesy buildup -> Night After Night.
Dives into the Arctic Ocean with cold plunderphonics before going full rave mode, working its way toward a colossal buildup that shatters through the surface and explodes like a hypergiant star.

song: The Way You Do the Things You Do
notes: Phases past underwater borders before firing upward and detaching into outer space.

Locked in grooving gives Cory space to toy with several synths before settling on the clavinet for speedy, funky playing that leaves behind a jazzy wake they dive into for several minutes of 1950s Latin jazz before taking things home.
A snappy, very well done take on the basic structure that incorporates several synth patches from previous outings, steps steadily, climbs for several big time buildups, and peaks spectacularly.
Absurdly funky.
Stuttery, staccato synthpop.
Great grand piano work that pokes in and out of a synth carousel.

Notably different in its approach than usual, featuring restrained guitar from Brian and egalitarian jamming that starts to bob and shuffle funkily before slipping into a misty, nocturnal, robotic groove that sprouts wishy-washy guitar and colorful keys as it drifts across lanes of previous versions, growing slicker as they traverse reflectively down the barren highway and ending with a supersonic peak.
A beautiful intro sets the stage for spacious, nocturnal, emotional trip hop that patiently reaches for new heights with bright, soulful jamming fronted by sprawling guitar.
Makes you want to run through a brick wall!
Features some feel-good, grimy, deeply funky swamp rock.

One of the best forays into synthpop for this song so far, anchored by a very strong Shon and progressing spectacularly and transcendently through the processes of maintenance leading up to an extended, explosive, incredible rocket launch of a peak.

Early incendiary guitar work from Brian paves the way for a consistently colorful, upbeat atmospheric funky wash that they cycle through before sliding into soapy synthpop, eventually slipping out for a dim coastal expedition that builds alongside a greyscale sunrise -> Night After Night.
Straightforward synthpop enters a dungeon connected with a colorful, pixelated cave system teeming with lush forestry, lakes, and streams that glitch and streak as a rave swallows the landscape.
Tropical rumblings, gliding keys, and swingy bass twang their way into an entrancing, cyclical, semi-electronic Afro-Cuban Funk river. Absolutely dialed in. Real precise ending, too!

Lasers groove through spacey waters as funk sirens conduct radar scans, locking together as syncopated fractals that morph through shapes before bouncing into an Afro-Cuban-Boogie blend that romps its way to a rocking ending.

Noticeably energetic guitar work pops up within the song itself, with rich synthpop sprouting quickly thereafter, bubbling, blinking, and phasing its way through an unexpectedly wonky buildup that soars to new heights with celebratory playing that radiates brightly and sprays rainbow mist before heading back to Motel 6 proper.
A longer than usual vocal jam and some minimalistic funk that grows grimy and loud for a big ending.

Another astounding second half of the song proper, this time with soulful guitar that grows mind-meltingly electrifying, followed by a confident dive into a cerulean synthpop pool that deepens in color as they swim through tunnels and between streams until brightening for an Allmans-y Southern Rock peak at its tail end.
Entrancing, groove-oriented jamming with a colossal peaking section that Brian slays with disgusting ferocity, and a genuine Salamander Song jam that fills the final stretch.
Deep funk first half that grooves down video game ravines before heating up.

Grooves speedily around the city, swaying in Soggy Froggy-dipped synth circles that loop around the Capital Beltway before sailing patiently along the Potomac with a cool, blue groove that swings psychedelic and bursts for a heated peak before touching down for Standing on the Moon (!) and then -> Windmill.
A determined take on the usual structure with good drumming from Nick throughout, cool atmospheric contributions from Cory, and a standout riff that Brian returns to a couple of times.
Afro Space Funk Odyssey Micro Jam.
Projects a raving oscilloscope onto an underwater second-story basement's dance floor.

Spacious, lush downtempo blooms quickly yet very naturally, setting the stage for encompassing, emotionally rich Neptunian bedroom pop, with mercurial raindrops falling on the tin roof overhead (credit: Mike in Austin), building triumphantly to a gigantic peak before hitting the main theme. Fantastic electric playing from Brian to start the second half, then a collective dive into New Wave, getting groovier as they sink deeper, then faster as they make their way back up the Potomac -> America.
Coasts past guyots and atolls before brightening. Very pretty throughout.
Settles within a lush tea garden similar to recent versions of Windmill (or 2/17/26 Todd's Tots) and closes out cleanly.
Rolls in a cyberpunk wheel around an electropop city lined with metallic aquariums until Cory jumps on the organ and they work their way through muddy caverns for a huge sunrise -> Galisteo Way.
Funkified, Type I jam with a very nice close.
Grooves steadily as one unit for a good bit.
Full stereo funky shuffle that goes through a brief, albeit delectable electronic phase before patiently building colorfully.
Another round of beautiful downtempo that space walks and twangs over the Midwest -> ETS.
Descends into a swirling pool lit by submerged electronics and eventually dives in for aquatic visualizer grooving that goes full-blown synthpop -> Enjoy the Silence.
Excellent encompassing synthpop with a grand, orchestral swell and release before closing out.
Tons of hard-hitting, emotional guitar packed in here.
Flickers through dungeon runs with watery guitar and unusual sample work before going full electropop, eventually breaking out into celebratory space that Brian demolishes.
Very, very well done.
Three distinct electronic parts to the jam, with the final third touching on beautifully bright, clean synthpop.

A completely new, exhilarating synth-focused take on the song itself, which poses the question of "what happens after transcending the Pursuit of Trance?" Answer: potentially this. Brilliantly bold, concentrated synthpop.
Finds itself in saturated organ-driven territory before getting into a cool, spacey buildup -> Mad World.
Cory gets and stays on the clav early, making for some swampy funk that gains an atmospheric trail as it zooms through barren desert, eventually heating up for a big peak.

Slower intro than usual, with a similar egalitarian presentation to the 2/21/26 version, this time opting for cohesive synthpop that quickly floats into an intergalactic ocean where flickering buoys leave colorful wakes as electronic waves wash over them before Brian goes off for a big ending.
Basks in sun-kissed, Allmans-y territory, building with sprawling guitar before dropping into an oceanic excursion that Cory leads with smooth synth work and sails cleanly -> Spunkadelic.
Starts and stays slower than usual, moving like molasses through iridescent interdimensional pathways with sampled synths, coalescing into gorgeous (borderline) Bitpop.
Finds itself in borderline Easy Listening, grand piano-tinged space where they drift for a solid couple of minutes in the second half.

Loops in a funky, slick '90s smooth jazz bubble for the first quarter before Shon gets out in front with overdriven bass and they swing into tasteful, metropolitan grooving that gets hot toward the end. More Funkadelic than Spunkadelic.
Cory gets out in front with sublime synth work in the first half and Brian tries to follow it up with some raging guitar in the second.
Fun first couple of minutes.
Superbly done! Incredible synths from Cory from 15:20 to 17:00.
Consistent throughout, with some very cool Shon, a Double Time-y trek past wormholes and through space, and a fiery ending that features Brian returning to the same riff from 3/5/26's Double Time.
Captivating, emotionally rich synthpop trip through the stars (literally).

Incorporates several High Beams samples, with the music flashing and acting as a vehicle switching between its high and low beams before firing its way down a starlit harbor toward a city, where it briefly connects with the main theme and drops into a very funky underground disco that works its way -> Ain't That Wrong.

Locked-in, syncopated grooving that quickly grows legs and takes off into a speedy, Acid Techno Cantaloupe Island rave jam that swings into a brief, jazzier passage before building to a modern, celebratory floor where Brian demolishes with several arena-filling peaks.
Speedy P-Funk grooving revolves into retro-futuristic electropop that fires into an excellent, powerful peak and subsequently soars away with surprising synths -> Digital Stardust.
Great build and close!
Entrancing, synth-adorned, sample-ridden, glitching deep funk.

Sets out surprisingly quickly for a deeply funky Wurlitzer (!) led jam, descending into a murky, aquatic groove that Cory drops samples on top of, then delivers some great synth work and a killer last few minutes from Brian.
Special Teams, Special Plays, Special Players. Brian shows up big time!
Two jams: the first staying in routine, feel-good, funky space, the second going into an underwater bunker that explodes into a colorful rave and heats up -> Motel 6.
Another good take on the now customary downtempo jam, this time with Shon stepping up and changing course for Peter Gabriel-y art pop that builds -> Mad World.
An incredible first few minutes from Brian, great Shon throughout, and a patient, airy, riff-oriented jam.

Mechanically glides around an intergalactic cryovolcano, speeding into a vibrant, McLovin-based rave and submerging for a cold groove that builds powerfully and bursts colorfully. WOW!!! Absolutely must hear!
Swims out to an intergalactic lapis lazuli ocean where new vocal samples, synths, and guitar shimmer as drums skip before brightening back toward the main theme.

Dances lightly around a spacious, dazzling ballroom for its first jam and digs into a laid-back, synth-fronted romp for its second. A bit of tinkering with new electronics, which ends up being hit or miss, but the last few minutes build beautifully -> Salamander Song.
Flies through intergalactic electronic Afro-Cuban oceans before drifting into deep space -> Tainted Love.
Spirited playing from Cory and Brian (seriously, Brian goes all out!) and flow state jamming that spreads out into beautiful electronic space -> The Lizards.
Locked-in grooving and Brian going Jersey Moss mode makes for a very well-rounded outing.
Spafford debut; performed in an alternative electronic style.
Coasts on a dark art pop groove similar to the previous night's Dissociation Assist until Cory busts out the electronics.
Cool version with a jazzy breakdown midway through.
Locked-in, entrancing jamming that coasts for a good while past neon-capped cliff divers until bursting colorfully. A truly dedicated effort.
Straightforward, mostly solid playing that touches on Gwen Stefani's 'Rich Girl.' Don't sleep on this ending!
Ridiculously funky, with an extra rave rendition tacked on at the end.
Brightens and breaks cleanly through several layers of clouds for a fantastic celebratory close.
A standout version that features the return of vocal samples and a terrific, Shon-fronted transition into electronic space.
Grooves patiently and funkily (not your standard ETS deal at all!) until Cory starts to spam samples and they move toward an enormous ending. Different!
Syncopated lava lamp grooving that churns around samples with slick keys before locking in on an Afro-Cuban naval expedition.
Dissonant and noisy.
Awesome, kick-ass New Wave intro that runs for nearly four minutes.
Wades in outer space for a few moments before exploding for a pristine peaking section.
